newsitem.title: ROMANIA: More stocks ready to join Romania OTC market.
newsitem.headline: More stocks ready to join Romania OTC market.

text.p: Another 48 Romanian companies are expected to join trading on the embryonic over-the-counter (OTC) market this week, bringing the total number of traded stocks to 78, the OTC system said on Monday.
The newcomers, all privatised under a mass selloff, include a farm machinery station, a brewer, a pharmaceutical company, oil product retailers, a sugar refinery and two shipyards.

The OTC trading system, the RASDAQ, was developed under a capital market project run by the U.S. Agency for International Development. It started last month with a pilot week of trading which ended with a modest turnover of 8.9 million lei.
Turnover climbed to more than 85 million lei last week, when the most heavily traded stock was IMEP SA electric motor maker, in which 247,156 shares changed hands at 274 lei.
Bijuteria SA jewellery maker was also in the focus. It traded some 8,000 shares at a 2,000 lei high early in the week.
The RASDAQ is expected eventually to trade shares in 5,000 firms, most of them turned private under the mass selloff which gave 15 million Romanians shares in exchange for vouchers.
Brokers expect OTC trading to gain ground as more companies sign up with the shareholders' register and join the market.
"It's just a matter of time before we see this market posting daily turnover levels higher than the stock exchange does in two weekly sessions," a system operator said.

The Bucharest bourse trades 14 stocks, of which only two are privately owned, and has had turnover levels of around 100 million lei in recent months. ($=3,450 lei) -- Luli Popescu, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
